The round-59 pin gate closes that hole as a pre-execution admission filter: byte-inequality, absence, or nonregularity of any declared executor source at the candidate forces non-admission. boundary_paragraph: tools/executor-source-pin.py is a bounded source-identity prerequisite, not an execution attestation. Given a verifier-supplied trusted commit and a candidate commit, it compares the raw Git blobs of declared regular executable-source paths and exits 0 only when all declared blobs are byte-equal, 1 (EXECUTOR_SOURCE_DRIFT) when a declared source differs, is missing, or is nonregular at the candidate, and 2 (EXECUTOR_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) on bad arguments, an invalid trusted commit/source, or an unresolvable candidate. It exists because round 58's C2 falsification showed a claimant-swapped executor (tools/registry-check.py) fabricating held/mutant tallies while the frozen counter still printed PASS: nothing bound the executed bytes to a trusted revision. Applied pre-execution, this gate rejects that forgery class at the declared-path level. It certifies nothing about execution, dependency or interpreter identity, completeness of the declared closure (undeclared bent helpers pass), or the trustworthiness of the verifier-supplied trusted revision itself; a cheat baked into the trusted bytes would be certified, not caught. Exit 0 authorizes the declared sources to be treated as the trusted sources for subsequent measurement; the honesty of that subsequent measurement remains the verifier's separate responsibility.
